haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If the order hasn't claimed it by then, the reservation is released and the stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, Order becomes REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is told which items are short, and Payment is never contacted.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key on each charge request, so the provider treats retries of that request as one charge.
haiku-low.q4: The customer is refunded the full amount by Payment, and the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with an email to the customer.
haiku-low.q5: Only when the OrderConfirmed event arrives, after the order is confirmed. On any failure the cart is left untouched so the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service coordinates the steps. Its order record, with its status, holds how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends an HTTP webhook to Payment, which then publishes events (PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined) that drive the other services.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores the id of every webhook it processes and ignores any repeat whose id is already stored.
haiku-low.q9: Order is set to PAYMENT_FAILED, and Inventory releases the reservation immediately, triggered by the PaymentDeclined event and then ReleaseStock, not by the 10-minute timer.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory tries to claim the stock. If the hold lapsed but stock is still free, the order is fulfilled. If the stock was sold, the claim fails and the customer is refunded.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is marked REFUND_PENDING in Payment's database and retried with backoff; a person is alerted if it keeps failing, and it is never dropped.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, sent after stock is claimed, causes the Cart service to empty the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If the order hasn't claimed it by then, it is released and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the customer is charged. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, the order is marked REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and the customer is told which items are short.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key: the order id is sent with every charge request, so the provider treats repeats as one request.
sonnet.q4: The customer is refunded the full amount by Payment, and the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and the customer is emailed.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on the OrderConfirmed event, after the order is CONFIRMED. On any failure the cart stays exactly as it was so the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: The Order service coordinates the steps, and the order's status (stored in Order's own database) records progress. Transitions between services are triggered by HTTP calls or events on the broker.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends an HTTP webhook to Payment. Payment then emits an event (PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined). On success, Inventory claims stock (StockClaimed event), then Order sets CONFIRMED.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores the id of every webhook it processes; a repeat finds its id already stored and is ignored.
sonnet.q9: Order becomes PAYMENT_FAILED and sends a ReleaseStock event, so Inventory releases the reservation right away rather than waiting for the 10-minute timer. The PaymentDeclined event triggers this.
sonnet.q10: On success Inventory tries to claim the stock. If the hold lapsed but the stock is still free, the claim succeeds and the order is fulfilled. If the stock was sold to someone else, the claim fails, the order is cancelled and the customer is refunded in full.
sonnet.q11: The refund is marked REFUND_PENDING in Payment's database and retried with backoff. If it keeps failing, a person is alerted. It is never dropped and is finished only once marked REFUNDED.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, emitted after Order sets CONFIRMED, is received by the Cart service, which empties the cart.
